verdict_reason: Mapping 403 to undefined correctly makes another organisation's notification show as 404 through currentJourney, and real.requests.test.js covers it, but the refusal is not logged.

todos.issue: The new HTTP_FORBIDDEN branch (lines 17-19) turns the backend's 403 for another organisation's notification into undefined and logs nothing. backendFetch logs only connection retries, and currentJourney (engine/journey.js:105-108) throws Boom.notFound without a log, so a cross-organisation read leaves no frontend trace with the journeyId. This is another service refusing what this one asked for, which the house rules say must log at warn. Lines 14-19 are also two branches with the same body.
todos.fix: Must: a 403 from the fulfilments GET logs once at warn with the journeyId and status before the caller sees it as not found, and the not-found and forbidden outcomes share one branch. One way: create a module logger with createLogger(), test response.status against [HTTP_NOT_FOUND, HTTP_FORBIDDEN] in a single condition, and in it call logger.warn({ journeyId, status: response.status }, 'Notification fulfilments refused by the backend') when the status is 403.
